context: a single passage from a letter by John Lubbock, which you are answering on its own
exchanges: As far as I know Kollikers paper on Chironomus & Leuckart’s on Melophagus are the only accounts we have of the embryology of the Diptera and in both these the embryo commences as an apod grub. The same is the case in Aphis and indeed it seems that while in the Crustacea the appendages appear rather before the segments, the reverse is the rule in Insects. Melophagus was supposed to be Pupiparous but Leuckart considers that the offspring is a larva. The case of Aphis is almost the same as that of the Orthoptera.

Very many thanks for your most useful note: I was quite in error about aphis.— I have stumbled on one of my M.S. reference to paper of L. Dufour, in Annal des Sc. (3d series) Tom 3. p. 79, in which he says, (if I have not misunderstood him) that in certain degraded Diptera, the ovarian vesicle assumes the shape “ebauche”, in the ovary, of the pupa:—(p. 87) “at no time assumes the form of larva”.— Would you be so very kind as to look at this paper, & give me your opinion when we meet on Saturday.
